_comment: RETIRED, HISTORICAL ONLY (#267) - do not revive. Moved into this retired/ subdirectory specifically so deploy_dashboards.sh's install loop (a non-recursive rules/elastic_watcher/*.json glob) stops attempting to PUT it - it was still being installed on every deployment before this move, despite being dead code since #220. soar_quarantine_alert v2 fired on three distinct detection paths; #220 superseded it as the LIVE /alert trigger with configs/logstash.conf's ingest-time HMAC-signed http output (see that file's Category 6 comment). #267 found the live replacement had only carried over 1 of these 3 conditions (the zeek.intel IOC-hit path) - the Scan::Port_Scan (T1046) and SSH brute-force (T1110) paths this file covers were silently dropped when it was superseded, leaving those two detections tagged for dashboards but never dispatched to automated response. Fixed by extending configs/logstash.conf's Category 6 condition (both the filter-stage signing block and the output-stage dispatch block - the two must stay in lockstep, see that file's own comments) to also fire on a T1110 pipeline tag, closing that gap in the architecturally-current place instead of reviving this Watcher (would duplicate HMAC signing logic in Painless, may hit a Watcher trial/Gold license wall per deploy_dashboards.sh's own comment, and risks a double-dispatch race between two independent live trigger paths). T1046 (Scan::Port_Scan) deliberately stayed dashboard-only, same as before this fix: security-auditor review found scan-detection.zeek fires on a bare SYN with no completed handshake, so wiring it into live dispatch (with no rate limiting anywhere in the /alert path) would have turned a spoofed-source SYN sweep into an automated-response amplifier against an attacker-chosen victim IP. Wiring T1046 in is deferred until #331 (a source-spoofing defense) exists. This file's own two original gaps (no HMAC signing, unconfirmed Watcher-parser handling of the _comment/_comment_paths keys) are now moot rather than fixed - it is no longer installed at all. Left in place as historical reference for the original 3-condition design, matching how configs/zeek/local.zeek was left as dead config with a header explaining why (#286) rather than deleted.
_comment_paths: 2. zeek.notice: Scan::Port_Scan notice fired by Zeek's scan detection policy
3. zeek.ssh: 5+ failed auth attempts from the same source IP in the last 1 min

script.source: // Prefer the top document hit (IOC or port-scan path); fall back to the top SSH brute-force IP if hits are zero. #220: also carry the MITRE technique ID through, for the agent's sliding host+technique suppression window - logstash.conf pipeline-tags Scan::Port_Scan as T1046 and the ssh_brute_force_candidates aggregation is definitionally always T1110 (there is no source doc to read a tag from in that branch, so it's set directly); the IOC (zeek.conn threat.indicator.domain) path has no pipeline technique tag today and is left '' - should_suppress_technique() treats an empty technique as never-suppress. def ip = 'unknown'; def mac = ''; def dataset = 'unknown'; def technique = ''; if (ctx.payload.hits.total.value > 0) { def src = ctx.payload.hits.hits[0]._source; if (src.containsKey('source')) { if (src.source.containsKey('ip'))  { ip  = src.source.ip; } if (src.source.containsKey('mac')) { mac = src.source.mac; } } if (src.containsKey('event') && src.event.containsKey('dataset')) { dataset = src.event.dataset; } if (src.containsKey('threat') && src.threat.containsKey('technique') && src.threat.technique.containsKey('id')) { technique = src.threat.technique.id; } } else { def buckets = ctx.payload.aggregations.ssh_brute_force_candidates.by_source_ip.buckets; if (buckets.size() > 0) { ip = buckets[0].key; dataset = 'zeek.ssh (brute-force)'; technique = 'T1110'; } } ctx.payload.soar_ip = ip; ctx.payload.soar_mac = mac; ctx.payload.soar_dataset = dataset; ctx.payload.soar_technique = technique; return ctx.payload;
